views.name: classroom_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom

params.description: Returns one row per classroom (building + room_number) with that room's capacity — answers questions about which individual rooms meet a capacity criterion or listing room capacities.
params.when_to_use: Find rooms whose capacity falls within a numeric range (e.g., list rooms with capacity between 50 and 100). | List all classrooms and their capacities (optionally filtered by building). | Use as a per-room dimension when composing aggregates if you explicitly aggregate capacity (e.g., SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building or AVG(capacity) GROUP BY building) after joining or grouping to the view's grain.
params.output_schema: building: classroom.building — building identifier | room_number: classroom.room_number — room identifier within building | capacity: classroom.capacity — seating capacity of the room
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity (direct column pass-through; per-room attribute at grain = building + room_number)
params.composition: Safe: join to one-row-per-building or one-row-per-(building,room_number) dimension tables on the matching keys; doing so preserves the per-room grain and does not duplicate capacity. | Unsafe: do not join directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., events, bookings) that have multiple rows per (building, room_number) without first aggregating the many-side or aggregating this view after the join. Otherwise capacity will be multiplied. | When composing building-level metrics from this view, explicitly aggregate capacity as appropriate (e.g., SUM(capacity) to get total capacity per building, AVG(capacity) for average room capacity).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not reuse when the question expects aggregated metrics across bookings/events that are at a different grain (e.g., total seats booked per building) without explicitly aggregating this view first — reason: this view is one-row-per-(building,room_number); joining it to a one-to-many events/bookings table without aggregation will duplicate capacities. | Do not reuse when the question requires attributes not present in this view (e.g., schedule, occupancy, or booking counts) — reason: the view only exposes building, room_number, and capacity. | Do not reuse when the correct join path requires a different cohort or filtered subset of classrooms (e.g., only rooms used in a particular term) because this view returns all rows from classroom without filters — reason: wrong cohort/grain for filtered cohorts.
params.dialect_notes: Dialect: SQLite — the SQL is simple SELECT from classroom; no dialect-specific functions used.

SELECT

  section.sec_id AS sec_id,
  section.semester AS semester,

  section.room_number AS room_number,

FROM section

params.description: Provides the classroom (building, room_number) and time_slot_id for each course section at the section grain (one row per course_id, sec_id, semester, year).
params.when_to_use: Find which building and room a specific section meets in given semester and year (filter by course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | List classroom assignments for all sections in a semester or year (group or filter by semester/year and then by building or room). | Combine with a classroom capacity or classroom metadata table that is one-row-per-(building, room_number) to report room capacities for each section (join on building, room_number).
params.output_schema: course_id: course identifier from section.course_id | sec_id: section identifier from section.sec_id | semester: term label from section.semester | year: year from section.year | building: building code/name from section.building | room_number: room identifier from section.room_number | time_slot_id: time slot reference from section.time_slot_id
params.grounded_columns: section.course_id | section.sec_id | section.semester | section.year | section.building | section.room_number | section.time_slot_id
params.metric: sections_per_building = COUNT(*) GROUP BY building  -- use COUNT(*) or COUNT(DISTINCT course_id, sec_id, semester, year) at the view's grain
params.composition: Safe: join to one-row-per-course or one-row-per-time_slot tables on course_id or time_slot_id because this view is one row per section and those joins preserve that cardinality. | Safe: join to a classroom metadata table that has one row per (building, room_number) to attach capacity or features without duplicating rows. | Not safe: direct joins to enrollments, meetings, schedule_changes, or other tables that have many rows per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — aggregate those tables to one row per section first (e.g., COUNT(student_id) GROUP BY course_id, sec_id, semester, year) before joining. | When aggregating downstream (e.g., sections_per_building), treat this view as atomic at the section grain to avoid double-counting after joins.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to count students or other events per section by directly joining an enrollments or meetings table — those are many-to-one to this view and will multiply rows. Instead, pre-aggregate enrollments/meetings to one row per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) before joining. | Do not use this view to infer schedules across multiple meeting instances per section (e.g., multiple meeting times stored in another table) because this view has one row per section and does not represent multiple meeting records — joining to a meetings table without aggregation will produce incorrect duplication. | Do not use this view as a section-level history/cohort if your downstream logic requires different grain (for example, per-student-per-section or per-meeting-instance) because the view's grain is strictly (course_id, sec_id, semester, year).
params.dialect_notes: SQL dialect: SQLite. The SQL is a single-table projection from section (no dialect-specific functions used).

views.name: classroom_counts_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count
FROM
  classroom
GROUP BY
  building

params.description: Provides the number of classroom rows aggregated at the building level (one row per building with a classroom count).
params.when_to_use: Get total count of classrooms in each building. | Compose higher-level reports that need classroom counts by building (e.g., join with building attributes to show capacity vs. number of classrooms). | Filter or rank buildings by how many classrooms they contain. | Use as a pre-aggregated source when joining to one-row-per-building dimensions to avoid re-counting classrooms.
params.output_schema: building: identifier of the building (sourced from classroom.building). This is the grouping key used in the view. | classroom_count: integer count of classroom rows in that building (derived from COUNT(*) over classroom rows grouped by classroom.building).
params.metric: classroom_count = COUNT(*) -- counts rows from the classroom table for each distinct classroom.building
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-building dimension (for example a building metadata view or table keyed by building) on classroom_counts_by_building.building = building_dim.building — safe because this view has exactly one row per building present in classroom, so classroom_count will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling view classroom_locations_with_capacity on building = classroom_locations_with_capacity.building is safe only if that sibling view is also one-row-per-building (verify its grain). If that view contains one row per building, counts will not be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example a sections table or any per-classroom or per-section detail) without re-aggregation, because joining a building-level aggregated view to rows that are multiple per building will multiply classroom_count and produce inflated measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many detail, either: (a) re-aggregate the detail to building-level before joining, or (b) join on building and then re-aggregate using SUM(classroom_count) grouped by the desired key while deduplicating building if needed. | do NOT join to classroom_core (which is normalized classroom rows) on classroom to enrich attributes at the classroom row level without re-aggregation. classroom_core is one-to-many relative to this view (many classroom_core rows per building), so a naive join will duplicate counts. If you must enrich classroom_count with classroom_core attributes, first aggregate classroom_core to one row per building (e.g., COUNT or other aggregates) then join. | when composing into larger queries, treat classroom_count as a building-level metric. Any join that preserves the one-row-per-building cardinality is safe; any join that expands rows per building requires re-aggregation of classroom_count to avoid double-counting.

views.description: Provides the number of classroom rows aggregated at the building level (one row per building with a classroom count).

views.name: department_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  building,
  budget
FROM
  department

params.description: Provides one row per department (dept_name) with its building and budget — useful for answering department-level attribute and budget questions.
params.when_to_use: Look up a department's building or budget by dept_name (e.g., "average budget for each department", "names and locations of top-funded departments"). | Compute department-level aggregates of budget (e.g., average or sum of budget across departments) — the view is already at the department grain so no re-aggregation of department rows is required. | Join department attributes into queries that are keyed at the department grain (dept_name), for example combining department budget with department-level classroom averages that have been pre-aggregated to dept_name.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department.dept_name (department name, one row per department) | building: department.building (building/location of the department) | budget: department.budget (department budget amount)
params.metric: budget = department.budget (raw stored budget column; can be aggregated across dept_name as AVG(department.budget), SUM(department.budget), etc.)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join to other one-row-per-department datasets on department.dept_name — this will not duplicate budget because both sides are keyed at dept_name. | When joining to many-sided data (classrooms, sections, etc.), first aggregate that data to department.dept_name (one row per dept) before joining to this view to avoid duplicating budget values. | When joining on building, ensure the counterpart is one-row-per-building (or aggregate it to one row per building) if you need to avoid multiplying department rows; otherwise prefer joining on dept_name.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining to many-to-one or many-to-many tables without first reducing the other side to department grain (e.g., raw classroom rows) if you expect a department-level budget to remain unduplicated — doing so will multiply department rows and thus duplicate budget values. Reason: the view returns one row per dept_name but has no protection against multiplicative joins from the other side. | Joining on building when the other dataset is many-rows-per-building and you expect department-level uniqueness preserved — if multiple departments share a building or the other side is many-per-building, joining directly can multiply department rows unless the other side is aggregated to one row per building. Reason: the view exposes building but does not encode that building is unique to a department.
params.dialect_notes: SQL dialect: SQLite — standard SELECT from a single table with no vendor-specific functions.

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.budget AS budget,
  d.budget - (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM department) AS budget_vs_avg_all_departments
FROM department d

params.description: Per-department budget and the difference between each department's budget and the average department budget.
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard that lists departments with their budgets and how each compares to the overall department average. | Composing a larger query that needs department-level budget measures as inputs (for further aggregation, ranking, filtering, or joins to department attributes). | Filtering or slicing by department while preserving a departmental budget measure that is already at department grain.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name) | budget: department budget (derived from department.budget) | budget_vs_avg_all_departments: department budget minus the average of department.budget across all department rows (derived from expression budget - AVG(department.budget) computed over the entire department table)
params.metric: budget = department.budget (base column, no aggregation in this view; one value per department row) | budget_vs_avg_all_departments = department.budget - (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM department) (expression: dept-level value minus scalar aggregate AVG(department.budget) computed over the entire department table)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_rows (SEL) on department.dept_name = department_rows.dept_name — safe because both this view and department_rows are one-row-per-department, so measures from this view are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a department-level dimension/view (one-row-per-department) on department.dept_name = <dim>.dept_name — safe because this view has one row per dept_name and will not be multiplied. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views such as section_classroom_mapping (JOIN) or classroom_core (NORM) without re-aggregation: those are one-to-many (a department can have many sections/classrooms), and joining them directly will multiply this view's rows/measures. If you need department-level measures combined with detail-level rows, first aggregate the detail table to department grain (e.g., COUNT or SUM grouped by department.dept_name) and then join to this view. | When composing further aggregations: treat budget as a measure at department grain. If you aggregate the composed result to a higher grain (e.g., school or campus) ensure you use aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, etc.) over this view's budget or budget_vs_avg_all_departments as appropriate; do not rely on row-count-preserving joins to maintain correct totals. | Because budget_vs_avg_all_departments subtracts a scalar AVG computed over the entire department table, it remains meaningful only at department grain. If you aggregate to a different grain, recompute the comparison against the appropriate aggregate (e.g., compare to the average within the aggregated group) rather than summing these per-department differences.

views.description: Per-department budget and the difference between each department's budget and the average department budget.

params.output_schema: dept_name: department.dept_name — department identifier (one row per dept_name) | building: department.building — department building/location | budget: department.budget — department budget | name_length: LENGTH(department.dept_name) — integer length of dept_name (computed in SQL using SQLite LENGTH)
params.metric: name_length = LENGTH(department.dept_name)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join to other one-row-per-dept_name views on dept_name (no duplication of budget/name_length). | Cardinality-safe: join to building-aggregated views on building only if the building-aggregated view is guaranteed to be one-row-per-building; otherwise aggregate the many-side first. | Unsafe without re-aggregation: do not join directly to course/section/classroom-level tables or other one-to-many relations keyed to dept_name; aggregate the many-side to department-level before joining, or join and then re-aggregate back to department grain to avoid duplicating department-level measures.

Reason: wrong grain for per-course/section answers.

FROM instructor i

params.description: Lists instructors along with their department name and salary (one row per instructor).
params.when_to_use: Fetch instructor-level details together with the canonical department row (e.g., reporting instructor name, ID, salary and department attributes). | Join instructor information to other one-row-per-department dimensions (e.g., department budget or building) without duplicating instructor measures. | Compose instructor-level filters or aggregations (e.g., average salary by department) using this view as the instructor grain source.

Avoid non-key joins that can produce many-to-many duplication.

views.name: top_instructor_per_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  i.ID AS "ID AS instructor_ID",
  i.name AS "name AS instructor_name",
  i.salary AS "salary AS instructor_salary",
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.dept_name ORDER BY i.salary DESC) AS rank_within_dept
FROM
  department d
JOIN
  instructor i
  ON i.dept_name = d.dept_name

params.description: For each department, returns instructors ordered by salary with a rank position (1 = highest paid) within that department.
params.when_to_use: Find the top-paid instructor(s) per department (e.g., rank_within_dept = 1). | Compare instructor salaries within the same department (e.g., top N by salary per department). | Join instructor-level department rankings to other tables when you need the single instructor rows (one row per instructor within their department) and the relative salary rank in their department. | Compose department-level summaries that need the identity and salary of the top instructor by selecting rank_within_dept = 1 and then aggregating across departments.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name) | ID AS instructor_ID: instructor identifier (derived from instructor.ID) | name AS instructor_name: instructor full name (derived from instructor.name) | salary AS instructor_salary: instructor salary amount (derived from instructor.salary) | rank_within_dept: rank position of the instructor's salary within the department (derived from RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department.dept_name ORDER BY instructor.salary DESC))

views.name: sections_with_classroom

SELECT

  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  c.capacity
FROM section_classroom_mapping AS s
JOIN classroom_core AS c

params.description: Provides section-level assignments to physical classrooms so you can answer which classroom (building, room) and its seating capacity is assigned to each course section in a given semester and year.
params.when_to_use: Find the classroom location and seating capacity for a specific course section (by course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | Aggregate or report classroom usage or capacity at the section grain (e.g., total capacity scheduled per semester). | Compose with course, instructor, or department views to analyze which sections (and their capacity) belong to which academic entities. | Filter or join to location-based resources (building-level summaries) while preserving one row per section.
params.output_schema: course_id: course identifier for the section — derived from section_classroom_mapping.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within the course — derived from section_classroom_mapping.sec_id | semester: academic term identifier (e.g., 'Fall') — derived from section_classroom_mapping.semester | year: calendar/academic year for the section — derived from section_classroom_mapping.year | building: building identifier where the section is scheduled — derived from section_classroom_mapping.building | room_number: room number within the building where the section is scheduled — derived from section_classroom_mapping.room_number | capacity: seating capacity of the assigned classroom — derived from classroom_core.capacity (joined by building+room_number)
params.grounded_columns: section_classroom_mapping.course_id | section_classroom_mapping.sec_id | section_classroom_mapping.semester | section_classroom_mapping.year | section_classroom_mapping.building | section_classroom_mapping.room_number | classroom_core.building | classroom_core.room_number | classroom_core.capacity

Safe because each view row already maps to a single classroom row, so measures (capacity, one-row-per-section) are not multiplied. | Safe to join to course or section master tables keyed to (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) (if such tables are one-row-per-section) because both sides share the same section grain — this preserves one row per section and does not duplicate capacities. | Safe to join to instructors_by_department or departments_basic only if those views/tables are known to be one-to-one with the section grain (e.g., a single instructor per section). If not guaranteed, first aggregate instructor relationships (e.g., choose_primary_instructor_per_section) before joining so you don't multiply section rows. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views (for example: a table of student enrollments, multiple meeting-times per section, or any schedule_changes log) without re-aggregation because those joins will duplicate rows and therefore duplicate the capacity measure. views.name: department_classroom_usages_for_prereq_free_courses
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  c.course_id AS course_id,

  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_prereq
